newsitem.title: USA: IBM to hire thousands in 97 - annual report.
newsitem.headline: IBM to hire thousands in 97 - annual report.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp said it plans to hire "thousands more" employees in 1997 to fuel growth, chairman and CEO Louis Gerstner said in the company's 1996 annual report.

In 1996, IBM's worldwide headcount grew to 241,000, up from 225,000 in 1995, mostly due to its fast-growing services business, an IBM spokesman said. In 1995, employment grew from 220,000 in 1994, the first time employment grew in 10 years.
IBM told analysts earlier this year that it will probably add as many new employees in 1997 as it did in 1996, with a big chunk in IBM Global Services group.
Earlier Wednesday, IBM said its Global Services business will become an IBM group, in part to reflect its growth and success. Services is now a $23 billion business.

"I'd like to add here that I am very happy -- and proud -- that our transformation has created job growth," Gerstner said in his letter to shareholders, in which he described 1996 overall as "a solid year."
When Gerstner first took over the then-struggling computer giant in April 1993, one of his first actions was to take a whopping restructuring charge and cut 25,000 jobs from IBM.

"Last year I told you that the transformation of IBM had progressed to the point where it was time for everyone in the company to focus on our strategic vision -- a networked world that transforms the way people work, interact, learn and do business," Gerstner wrote. "And, I said, implementing this strategic vision would fuel future IBM growth."

IBM's revenues grew for the second consecutive year, up six percent in 1996 and up nine percent after adjusting for the effects of currency changes -- its highest growth since 1985. But its earnings were primarily flat due to weakness in Europe and declining memory chip prices.
"We're not happy with flat earnings," Gerstner said, but he also pointed out that IBM's stock price rose 66 percent in 1996 and, as a result, IBM's market value grew $27 billion.
"That brings the total increase since our major restructuring in 1993 to more than $50 billion," he said.

"I believe that we have made enormous progress over the last four years -- in part because of the grit and determination and talent and teamwork of IBM employees -- and also because we set a strategic direction for the company that was right for us, right for our industry and, most importantly, right for our customers."
Gerstner said that, while other CEOs might be tempted at that point in their annual letter to shareholders to announce some new bold direction, he was resisting the temptation.
"I believe we should stay the course," he said.

He said network computing is changing where computing takes place and how computing is used. It also improves the efficiences and speed between companies, business partners and others. IBM is adapting and enabling every hardware and software product in its portfolio for the Internet, he said.
IBM said its annual report will be live on its World Wide Web site on Thursday, with audio and other features.
Gerstner reads his letter to shareholders, which will also have translations into six other languages later this week.

The site also includes areas, where users can look up the financial report, historical charts (with an interactive area to compare areas of the financial reports) and understanding financials. IBM's annual report can be found Thursday on the Internet at www.ibm.com/AnnualReport/1996.
